prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip supports a coarse near–far layout: the camera wearer's arms and torso occupy the nearest region at roughly 0.2–0.8 m, while benches, bicycles, cabinets and walls span approximately 1–5 m away. Across the five frames, the view turns from the workbench and nearby person on the left toward the bicycles, glass doors and open floor ahead/right; the bright near-field arm regions shift correspondingly across the image. Large dark areas generally indicate more distant floor, doors or furniture, and brightness boundaries help separate overlapping foreground limbs from the room even where RGB textures are cluttered. Metric distances are only rough because the map is monocular, heavily smoothed, and sometimes assigns inconsistent depth to walls, doors, limbs and frame edges.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only a few regions: several pink person masks correspond mainly to the camera wearer's partly visible arms/body in the later frames, while other people and most workshop objects are missed. These masks show that the wearer's limbs are low in the view, partly out of frame, and within arm's reach, but they do not reliably establish the distance or facing direction of other people. The labelled green sports-ball region is a small object around the left-centre frames, whereas the huge green clock region and tiny car region do not match the RGB scene plausibly and are unreliable spatial evidence. Over time, the pink masks move from the lower centre toward the right as the wearer turns, making foreground occlusion clearer than in RGB, but the sparse and erroneous detections prevent a complete account of object-to-object distances.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no detected body or hand joints, facing direction, gaze direction, reach geometry or person-to-person spacing. It therefore cannot clarify whether the nearby person in the early left-side view faces or looks toward the camera wearer, nor can it track any approach, retreat or turning. The absence of skeletons is unreliable as evidence that no people or hands are present, because the RGB and segmentation strips visibly contain foreground limbs and at least a partly visible person. Likely spatial difficulties for the detector include severe cropping, egocentric perspective, motion blur and occlusion, but the map itself provides no positive spatial facts beyond the failure to localize poses.
